subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: Should OpenClaw make structured `toolCall`/`toolUse` protocol objects the only default executable tool boundary, or continue allowing standalone assistant text promotion for local-model compatibility?
rationale: Both directions are plausible: strict execution improves security and provenance, while current promotion preserves documented compatibility for local models that emit text-shaped tool calls.

options.title: Strict protocol by default
options.body: Assistant text would remain text unless an explicit, auditable compatibility path opts into repair and promotion.

options.title: Keep compatibility promotion
options.body: The current promotion behavior would remain supported, with this issue narrowed to docs, warnings, and targeted `tool_choice` guidance.

options.title: Defer to response gates
options.body: The broader enforcement design would move to the pre-response gate work in #13583 instead of changing the default tool boundary now.

recommendation.title: Strict protocol by default
recommendation.body: Assistant text would remain text unless an explicit, auditable compatibility path opts into repair and promotion.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent-runtime work touched the shared tool-call terminal contract and is the closest available owner signal for a cross-runtime security-boundary decision.
